occupants.note: ADOPTED BY THE INFERRED-HOUSEHOLD PROGRAMME (docs/ROADMAP.md K1, phase two). This anonymous roof is the workplace of an inferred shoemaker's household (3 of 3 this layer infers): hh_inf_shoemaker_north_03 in data/residents/households/. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit. The occupant is hypothesised from the town's demonstrable needs - the 1835 census of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings against the trades Andreas's 1833 roster names - and is not a person: no name is claimed and no figure is drawn.

persons.name: A shoemaker (inferred resident, unnamed)
persons.note: HYPOTHESISED, AND NOT A PERSON. No source names this resident and none is claimed to: the record asserts that a town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings held at least this many households of this trade, and asserts nothing whatever about any individual. The name field carries a designation because inventing a surname would make this record indistinguishable at a glance from the documented layer beside it. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). THE THIRD OF 3 SHOEMAKER HOUSEHOLDS THIS LAYER INFERS. Three thousand two hundred and sixty-five people wear out boots in a town whose streets are mud for half the year, and the nearest bench otherwise is Detroit. The schedule allows six W4 small artisan shops; three shoemaking households are inferred, one of them working from an anonymous shop roof already on the plat.

residents.research_note: INFERRED HOUSEHOLD - third of 3 shoemaker households in this layer, in the north division. Three thousand two hundred and sixty-five people wear out boots in a town whose streets are mud for half the year, and the nearest bench otherwise is Detroit. The schedule allows six W4 small artisan shops; three shoemaking households are inferred, one of them working from an anonymous shop roof already on the plat. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.
